accounts.canonical_name: Limitation for Title XVIII of the Social Security Act
accounts.agency: Department of Health and Human Services
accounts.notes: A general-provision line printed only for FY2026 Enacted (the JES and H.Rept. 119-696 p.392, 2,000; '---' in the FY2027 columns). The provision of P.L. 119-75 it reflects is not identified here -- the Title II general provisions carry no section naming title XVIII with that figure; to be confirmed. Vision read H.Rept. 119-696's label as 'mitation ...' (the page image prints 'Limitation ...'). The FY2026 line is P.L. 119-75 Division B sec. 241 (PDF p.120, 140 Stat. 293): CMS shall not apply the distance requirements of SSA sec. 1820(c)(2)(B)(i)(I) to certain critical access hospitals -- a title XVIII provision the FY2026 explanatory statement lists as 'a new provision related to title XVIII of the Social Security Act' (p.245) and its table scores at 2,000 (p.296). Not in the FY2021 or FY2022 bills, Budget Appendix language or laws (searched for '1820(c)(2)(B)' and 'distance requirement'). Its confirmed absences, which rested on tables' silence, were retired 2026-10-08 (owner).

Confirm whether budget authority alone captures the FY27 CHIMP / CHIMP Pop-Up mechanism correctly
validations.observed_result: The CBO document's own multi-year spendout table shows the FY27 CHIMP Pop-Up (BA $0 in FY2027) carries a +$2,670,000,000 BA entry in FY2028 -- a single-year budget authority field doesn't represent this restoration. May need a dedicated CHIMP amount_type and/or a multi-year scorekeeping note field.
validations.resolution: Deprioritized, not resolved. CHIMPs are a mandatory-spending mechanism by definition, and the Crime Victims Fund entry here is mandatory trust-fund plumbing, not a discretionary account. Given the platform is focused on discretionary accounts, a dedicated amount_type or multi-year scorekeeping field is not worth building for this. Left documented for historical accuracy; not blocking Step 3.

Proposed type, from explicit text: split_from -- FY2024 Budget Appendix (BUDGET-2024-APP, HHS chapter granule BUDGET-2024-APP-1-10, PDF pp. 59 and 64): 'The 2024 Budget requests resources for the Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response (ASPR) in a new account, separate from PHSSEF where funding has historically been appropriated.' P.L. 117-328 (FY2023) funds the preparedness programs under the Office of the Secretary's 'Public Health and Social Services Emergency Fund' heading (p.419); P.L. 118-47 (FY2024) has no such heading and an 'Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response' with this heading (p.211). Confirmed by the owner's test (2026-10-08), run on the first restated year: the FY2023 reports' FY2022 column prints no ASPR structure ('Total, PHSSEF' 3,199,678: H.Rept. 117-403 p.836; the FY2023 Senate draft p.419), so the FY2024 report's FY2023 column was used: S.Rept. 118-84 restates FY2023 as ASPR 3,629,677 (Research, Development, and Procurement 3,062,991 + Operations, Preparedness, and Emergency Response 566,686; pp.389-390) + a residual PHSSEF 137,892 (p.392) = 3,767,569 (thousands), exactly the FY2023 law's PHSSEF paragraphs (P.L. 117-328 div. H: $1,647,569,000 + $820,000,000 + $965,000,000 + $335,000,000 = $3,767,569,000). Through FY2023 ASPR's programs were funded within PHSSEF: P.L. 117-328 appropriates them under its PHSSEF heading (owner, 2026-10-09: Enacted follows the law; ASPR's FY2023 Enacted figures, S.Rept. 118-84's restatement, retired). Note: Funded within PHSSEF before FY2024. Cell note (ACC-HHS-ASPR-RDP FY2023 Enacted): S.Rept. 118-84 restates FY2023 in the FY2024 structure (ASPR separate from PHSSEF): 3,062,991 thousand (p.389).
